cleanIntro: ⛔ The EVO SP is the one striker pistol in this group that does NOT need the trigger pulled to come apart — Kimber says so in a note above the procedure. It also takes a small punch to start the slide stop, which is worth having on the bench before you begin rather than after.

steps.title: Unloaded, inspected — and no trigger pull needed
steps.action: Magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty by eye. ⛔ Read the note before you go further: there is NO need to pull the trigger to strip an EVO SP. If a procedure you half-remember says to, it is another pistol's procedure.
steps.aside: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring is under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury, property damage or loss.
steps.quote: There is no need to pull the trigger for disassembly of the EVO SP.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Magazine free, then line the tab up with the notch
steps.action: Support hand under the grip, thumb on the magazine release — it is on either side of the frame behind the trigger — and let the magazine drop free. Then pull the slide rearward until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop lines up with the semi-circular notch in the slide.
steps.quote: Pull the slide rearward until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop is aligned with the semi-circular notch in the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Small punch pushes the slide stop out from the RIGHT
steps.action: Use a small punch or pin to push the slide stop out from the right side of the frame. This one genuinely wants a tool; a fingernail will not start it and forcing it with a screwdriver marks the frame.
steps.quote: Use a small punch or pin to push the slide stop out from the right side of the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Slide, barrel and spring off the front as one
steps.action: Pull the slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly forward off the front of the frame together. Nothing is loose yet.
steps.quote: Pull the slide, barrel, and recoil spring assembly off the front of the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Cam block off the spring, then the barrel — strip complete
steps.action: Push from the REAR of the cam block toward the muzzle and lift slightly, then pull the cam block back and off the recoil spring, and draw the spring out toward the rear of the slide. Lift the barrel and move it rearward out of the slide. Kimber stops the owner here.
steps.aside: The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning.
steps.quote: Remove the cam block and recoil spring assembly by pushing from the rear of the cam block towards the muzzle and lifting up slightly.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: The cleaning rod enters at the chamber, never the muzzle. Wet patch with bore solvent, let it soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose debris — and read the solvent maker's own directions, because some of them will lift a finish as happily as they lift fouling.
steps.aside: Run a patch wet with bore cleaning solvent through the barrel and let the solution soak a few minutes.
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Wet brush through and OUT the muzzle, then repeat to clean
steps.action: Push the wet bore brush in at the chamber and all the way OUT of the muzzle before drawing it back — reversing a brush inside the bore folds the bristles over. Dry patch after, and repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean. Then a light oil, and ⛔ a dry patch through before you ever fire it.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face and every bearing surface — nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on the slide and frame, then get into the breech face and the rest of the parts with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. ⛔ And no ultrasonic tank: Kimber says damage from one is not covered by warranty, and night sights must never go near it.
steps.aside: Do not expose night sights to an ultrasonic cleaning environment.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, at the points Kimber names
steps.action: Premium oil, not grease — and if it carries Teflon, shake it, because the Teflon settles overnight and you will otherwise apply the carrier and none of the additive. Then oil only where this book says, in the quantities it gives.
steps.aside: Barrel hood; 2 drops spread across surface
steps.quote: Slide and frame rails; 3 drops on each side
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel, and wipe the excess
steps.action: Reassemble, work the slide five or six times, dry fire, then wipe off the excess. Moderation is the whole point: too little and it wears, too much and it collects the grit that wears it faster. ⛔ And if it has been stored oiled, a dry patch goes through the barrel before firing.
steps.quote: If the firearm has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, push a dry patch through the barrel before firing.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Recoil spring is a scheduled part — 3,000 rounds
steps.action: Kimber publishes a replacement interval for the EVO SP's recoil spring: every 3,000 rounds, and MORE often if you shoot +P. A tired recoil spring on a small striker pistol shows up as brass in your face and failures to go into battery long before it shows up as a broken part.
steps.aside: Always slide the recoil spring down the guide rod until seated against the base of the guide rod.
steps.quote: recoil spring after every 3,000 rounds. If you use +P ammunition you may need to replace the spring more frequently to maintain proper function.
steps.cite: Kimber EVO SP Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION / MAINTENANCE

deepAbsentReason: Kimber's limit is printed in the strip itself — "The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning." — and again as a warning: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." Going further voids the warranty in Kimber's own words. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel into the slide, entered from above and moved forward.
Recoil spring down the guide rod until seated against the base; cam block back onto the spring.
Cam block and spring assembly into the slide.
Slide, barrel and spring assembly onto the frame rails from the front.
Slide drawn back until the tab meets the notch, slide stop pressed in from the left and seated.
Cycle the slide, dry fire, wipe off excess lubrication.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: work the slide five or six times and confirm it goes fully into battery, then dry fire and wipe off the excess oil. Check the slide stop is fully seated from the left. ⛔ If the recoil spring is round wire with one open and one closed end, the CLOSED end goes on the guide rod first, open end toward the muzzle.
